mainTopic: Tearing clothes and honoring the dead, especially a חכם, with stories of the funerals of רב ספרא, רב הונא and רב חסדא
overview: The משנה taught that only relatives tear their clothes over a death. The גמרא narrows this step by step. Everyone tears for a חכם, everyone tears for an אדם כשר, and anyone present at the moment of death must tear. So the משנה covers only someone who was none of these, when the person was not there at the death. Then come stories that teach how to honor a חכם who died. אביי tells the חכמים to tear for רב ספרא at his הספד. רב חסדא directs רב הונא's funeral: no ספר תורה on the bier, out through the doorway, and on his first bier. רב הונא is eulogized and brought to ארץ ישראל, where the גמרא settles two ברייתות about honoring a coffin, and he is buried beside רבי חייא. The amud closes with רב חסדא's funeral and the start of the story of רבה בר הונא and רב המנונא, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Does the rule apply even to a Torah scholar?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the משנה's rule, that only relatives tear, applies even when a חכם dies. It quotes a ברייתא that says everyone is his relative.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Does this apply even to a חכם? But a ברייתא teaches: when a חכם dies, everyone is his relative.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's rule that only relatives tear their clothes. It points to a ברייתא that says that when a חכם dies, everyone counts as his relative.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה limited tearing and the other mourning acts to relatives. The ברייתא seems to widen this, at least for a חכם, to everyone. So the two sources appear to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא? (opens a challenge)

phrases.english: GEMARA: And even a Sage?
phrases.notes: He means: does the משנה's rule that only relatives tear apply even when a חכם dies?

phrases.english: But isn't it taught:
A Sage who died: everyone is his relative.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the discussion of the משנה's rule that only relatives tear.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that only relatives tear and mourn.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says that when a חכם dies, everyone counts as his relative. That contradicts limiting the mourning acts to actual relatives.

steps.title: Rereading the ברייתא: everyone is like a relative
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says that 'everyone is his relative' cannot be literal. The ברייתא must mean everyone acts like a relative: tearing, baring the shoulder, and eating the mourner's meal. This keeps the challenge alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really think everyone is literally his relative? Rather, everyone is like his relatives: everyone tears over him, everyone bares the shoulder over him, and everyone eats the mourner's meal over him in the town square!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes how to read the ברייתא it just quoted. It shows that the ברייתא really does mean everyone does the mourning acts, so the challenge against the משנה still stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nobody literally becomes a relative of the חכם. So the ברייתא is read as 'like his relatives.' It then lists the exact acts the משנה limited to relatives: tearing, baring, and the mourner's meal. That makes the clash with the משנה even sharper.

keyTerms.meaning: Can it enter your mind? (this cannot be meant literally)
They tear their garments in mourning
They bare the shoulder in mourning
They serve or eat the mourner's first meal (סעודת הבראה)

phrases.english: Everyone is his relative, can that enter your mind?!
Rather: everyone is like his relatives:
everyone tears over him,
and everyone bares the shoulder over him,
and everyone eats the mourner's meal over him in the square!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the wording of the ברייתא quoted in step 1 and completes the challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's limit of mourning acts to relatives.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Read correctly, the ברייתא says everyone tears, bares, and eats the mourner's meal for a חכם. These are the very acts the משנה says only relatives do.

steps.title: The משנה is about someone who was not a scholar
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה is talking about a person who was not a חכם.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed for a case where he is not a Sage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It narrows the משנה so that it only covers someone who was not a חכם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no real contradiction, because each source covers a different case. The ברייתא is about a חכם, where everyone mourns. The משנה's rule that only relatives mourn applies to someone who was not a חכם.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for... (limits a ruling to a specific case)

phrases.english: No, it is needed
where he is not a Sage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 1 and 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): the משנה covers a non-scholar.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to say that only relatives tear even for a חכם.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה covers only someone who was not a חכם. For a חכם, everyone mourns.

steps.title: Even for an upright person, everyone must tear
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again: even if he was not a חכם but was an אדם כשר, everyone should have to tear. It brings a ברייתא that says children die young so that the parent will cry and mourn over an upright person.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he was an upright person, one is obligated to tear. As a ברייתא teaches: why do a person's sons and daughters die when they are young? So that he will cry and mourn over an upright person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new challenge to the answer it just gave. Even a non-scholar who was an אדם כשר seems to require everyone present to tear, and the גמרא brings a ברייתא to show it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 3 left room for any non-scholar. But the ברייתא shows that mourning an upright person is extremely important. So the משנה's rule would still clash in the case of an אדם כשר. The wording of this ברייתא will be questioned in the next step.

phrases.english: And if he is an upright person
one is obligated to tear.
As it is taught:

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי מָה בָּנָיו וּבְנוֹתָיו שֶׁל אָדָם
phrases.english: For what reason do a person's sons and daughters
die when they are young?

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּבְכֶּה וְיִתְאַבֵּל עַל אָדָם כָּשֵׁר.
phrases.english: So that he will cry and mourn over an upright person.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אָדָם כָּשֵׁר הוּא חַיּוֹבֵי מִיחַיַּיב לְמִיקְרַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 3, which allowed the משנה's rule for any non-scholar.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the משנה covers anyone who is not a חכם.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An אדם כשר is not a חכם, yet mourning him is so important that everyone present should tear. So the משנה cannot cover every non-scholar.

steps.title: Questioning the wording: is a pledge taken in advance?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the ברייתא's wording. Would children die in advance, like a security deposit, to make sure the parent mourns later?
steps.simpleTranslation: So that he will cry and mourn?! Is a security pledge being taken from him?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to question the wording of the ברייתא it just quoted. Punishing someone ahead of time for something he has not done makes no sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'So that he will mourn' sounds like the children are taken in advance as a guarantee for future behavior. That is unreasonable. So the ברייתא's wording must be reread, which the next step does.

phrases.english: He will cry and mourn?!
Is a security pledge being taken from him?!

steps.triggerLanguage: יִבְכֶּה וְיִתְאַבֵּל עֶרְבוֹנָא קָא שָׁקֵיל מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side challenge on the wording of the ברייתא quoted in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's wording 'so that he will cry and mourn.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Children would not die ahead of time as a guarantee of future mourning. Punishment does not come in advance.

steps.title: Corrected reading: because he did not mourn
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא means the children die because the parent failed to cry and mourn over an upright person. Whoever does mourn him is forgiven for all his sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: because he did not cry and mourn over an upright person. For anyone who cries and mourns over an upright person is forgiven for all his sins because of the honor he showed him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rereads the ברייתא so that it makes sense: the children's death is a punishment for not mourning. This reading also brings back the challenge from step 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this fix, the punishment comes after the failure, not before it. The ברייתא adds that mourning an אדם כשר earns forgiveness of all sins. That shows how serious this mourning is, so everyone should tear for an אדם כשר, and the challenge to the משנה stands.

phrases.english: Rather: because he did not cry and mourn
over an upright person.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכׇּל הַבּוֹכֶה וּמִתְאַבֵּל עַל אָדָם כָּשֵׁר
phrases.english: For anyone who cries and mourns over an upright person
is forgiven for all his sins
because of the honor he showed him!
phrases.notes: Him means the upright person who died.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מִפְּנֵי שֶׁלֹּא בָּכָה וְהִתְאַבֵּל עַל אָדָם כָּשֵׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording question of step 5 and brings back the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The children die in advance so that the parent will mourn later.
steps.terutzMaskana: The children die because the parent failed to mourn an upright person. Mourning him earns forgiveness of all sins.

steps.title: The משנה is about someone who was not upright
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה is talking about a person who was not an אדם כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where he is not an upright person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from steps 4 and 6. It narrows the משנה even further: only relatives tear for someone who was not an אדם כשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same kind of answer as step 3, but the case is now narrower. For a חכם or an אדם כשר, everyone mourns. The משנה's limit to relatives covers only someone who was neither.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's rule that only relatives tear applies only when the one who died was neither a חכם nor an אדם כשר. For a חכם everyone acts like a relative, and everyone present tears for an אדם כשר, whose mourners are forgiven for their sins.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean an ordinary person is not mourned at all. His relatives still tear and mourn fully. The point is only that people who are not his relatives are not required to.

phrases.english: Where he is not an upright person.
phrases.notes: The גמרא leaves out 'it is needed'; it means the משנה is talking about such a case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 4 and 6.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה covered any non-scholar, including an אדם כשר.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה covers only someone who was not an אדם כשר.

steps.title: Someone present at the moment of death must tear
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again: even for a person who was not a חכם and not an אדם כשר, anyone standing there when the soul leaves must tear. It proves this from a ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he was standing there when the soul left, he must tear! As a ברייתא teaches: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says, one who stands over the dead person when the soul leaves must tear. It is like a burned ספר תורה, over which one must tear.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises one more challenge to the משנה, which seems to say that some people do not tear. It points out that anyone present at the moment of death must tear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 said the משנה is about someone who was not an אדם כשר. But the ברייתא says being present at death creates its own duty to tear, no matter who died. So the משנה's case still needs a tighter definition.

keyTerms.meaning: the moment the soul leaves the body, the moment of death
one who stands over the dead person, someone present at the death
to tear one's clothes as a sign of mourning
a Torah scroll that was burned

phrases.english: But if he was standing there
at the time the soul departs
he is obligated!
phrases.notes: Obligated to tear his clothes, even though the dead person was not a relative, a חכם, or an אדם כשר.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא:
Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
One who stands over the dead person
at the time the soul departs
is obligated to tear.
To what is this similar?
To a Torah scroll that was burned,
over which one is obligated to tear!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי דְּקָאֵי הָתָם בִּשְׁעַת יְצִיאַת נְשָׁמָה חַיּוֹבֵי מִיחַיַּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 7 by adding another situation where everyone must tear.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the משנה speaks of someone who was not an אדם כשר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Being present at death creates a duty to tear no matter who died, so the משנה's case still cannot be one where no one tears.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר comparing it to a burned ספר תורה

steps.title: The משנה is about someone not present at death
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה speaks of someone who was not standing there when the soul left.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה is talking about someone who was not standing there when the soul left.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final answer: the משנה's case is someone who was not present at the moment of death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Put all the answers together: the משנה is about a person who was not a חכם, not an אדם כשר, and the listener was not there when he died. Only then is there no duty to tear.
steps.whatToRemember: No קריעה is required only if the dead person was not a relative, not a חכם, not an אדם כשר, and you were not present at the death.

phrases.english: Where he was not standing there
at the time the soul departs.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּלָא קָאֵי הָתָם בִּשְׁעַת יְצִיאַת נְשָׁמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8 by narrowing the משנה's case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה might include someone present at the death.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה speaks only of someone who was not present at the moment of death.

steps.title: The חכמים did not tear for רב ספרא
steps.stepSummary: A story: when רב ספרא died, the חכמים did not tear their clothes, saying they had not learned from him.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב ספרא died, the חכמים did not tear for him. They said: we did not learn from him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story about real-life קריעה. It is setting up אביי's correction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים assumed you only tear for a חכם if he was your own teacher. Since רב ספרא did not teach them, they thought there was no duty.

keyTerms.meaning: his soul rested, he passed away
an אמורא who was a great חכם
we did not learn from him

phrases.english: When Rav Safra passed away,
the Rabbis did not tear over him.
They said: We did not learn from him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new section: a story applying the rule of tearing for a חכם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים held that one tears only for a חכם who was one's own teacher.

steps.title: אביי: you tear for any חכם, and you did learn from him
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects their reasoning: the ברייתא says 'a חכם who died', not 'a teacher who died'. Also, they repeat רב ספרא's teachings every day in the בית מדרש.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to them: Does the ברייתא say 'a teacher who died'? It says 'a חכם who died'. And besides, every day his teachings are in our mouths in the בית מדרש.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי tells the חכמים they were wrong not to tear, and gives two reasons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First reason: the rule is about any חכם, not only your own teacher. Second reason: even if it were only for a teacher, they learn רב ספרא's Torah daily, so he counts as their teacher.

phrases.english: Abaye said to them:
Is it taught 'A teacher who died'?
It is taught 'A חכם who died.'
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא from earlier in the sugya that requires tearing over a חכם.

phrases.english: And furthermore: every day
his teachings are in our mouths
in the study hall.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ אַבָּיֵי: מִי תַּנְיָא הָרַב שֶׁמֵּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reasoning the חכמים gave in step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The חכמים's claim that they had no duty to tear for רב ספרא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: They misread the ברייתא as 'teacher' instead of 'חכם', and they did in fact learn from him daily.

steps.title: It is not too late while the הספד goes on
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים thought the chance to tear had passed. אביי quotes a source: for a חכם, people must tear as long as they are busy with his הספד.
steps.simpleTranslation: They thought: what happened, happened. אביי said to them: We learned, for a חכם, as long as people are busy with the הספד, they must tear.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים accept that they should have torn, but think it is now too late. אביי shows them it is not too late.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally tearing happens at the time of death or when hearing the news. For a חכם, the duty lasts as long as the הספד is still going on.

keyTerms.meaning: what happened, happened; it's too late

phrases.english: They thought: What happened, happened.
Abaye said to them: We learned:
A חכם: as long as people are busy with the eulogy,
they are obligated to tear.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After accepting they should tear, the חכמים think it is too late; אביי rejects that.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The assumption that the time for tearing had passed
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: For a חכם, the duty continues as long as the הספד is going on.

steps.title: Tear at the time of the הספד, not right away
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים wanted to tear immediately. אביי told them a חכם's honor is at his הספד, so they should wait and tear then.
steps.simpleTranslation: They thought to tear right away. אביי said to them: A ברייתא teaches, a חכם's honor is at his הספד.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים rush to tear on the spot, and אביי gives the last correction: wait for the הספד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tearing is part of honoring the חכם. Doing it at the הספד, in front of everyone, gives him the most honor.

keyTerms.meaning: his honor is at his eulogy

steps.whatToRemember: For a חכם: you tear even if he was not your teacher, it is not too late while the הספד is going on, and the best time to tear is at the הספד itself.

phrases.english: They thought to tear immediately.
Abaye said to them: It is taught in a ברייתא:
A חכם, his honor is at his eulogy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Corrects the חכמים's overreaction to step 12 and sets the proper timing.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The קריעה for a חכם should be done at the time of his הספד, because that is where his honor is.

steps.title: When רב הונא died, they wanted to put a ספר תורה on his bier
steps.stepSummary: A new story begins. After רב הונא died, the people planned to place a ספר תורה on his bier.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב הונא died, they thought to place a ספר תורה on his bier.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story about רב הונא's funeral. This line sets up the first plan, which רב חסדא will push back on in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting a ספר תורה on a חכם's bier was a way to honor him. The story is built as a pattern: the people suggest something, and רב חסדא corrects them. This is the first suggestion.

keyTerms.meaning: Bed, or a bier for carrying the dead

phrases.english: When Rav Huna died,
they thought to place a Torah scroll on his bier.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new funeral story after the story of רב ספרא in steps 10-13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The people planned to honor רב הונא by placing a ספר תורה on his bier.

steps.title: רב חסדא objects: don't do for him what he didn't hold of while alive
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says it makes no sense to do something for רב הונא after his death that he did not agree with during his life.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said to them: Something he did not hold of during his life, should we now go and do it for him?
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא rejects the plan to put a ספר תורה on the bier. His reason: רב הונא himself did not approve of this kind of thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is that you honor a person in his own way, not against his own view. If רב הונא would not have wanted it, it is no honor to him. The next step brings proof of what רב הונא's view was.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said to them:
A thing that in his lifetime he did not hold of,
now should we stand up and do it for him?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב חִסְדָּא: מִילְּתָא דִּבְחַיֵּיהּ לָא סְבִירָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the plan from step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The plan to place a ספר תורה on רב הונא's bier.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It goes against רב הונא's own view, so it is not a real honor to him.

steps.title: Proof from רב תחליפא: רב הונא would not sit on a bed with a ספר תורה on it
steps.stepSummary: רב תחליפא saw רב הונא move a ספר תורה off his bed onto an upside-down jug before sitting down. This shows רב הונא held it is forbidden to sit on a bed with a ספר תורה on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב תחליפא said: I saw רב הונא, who wanted to sit on his bed, and a ספר תורה was lying on it. He turned a jug upside down on the ground and placed the ספר תורה on it. So he holds: it is forbidden to sit on a bed that has a ספר תורה lying on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רב חסדא with a story showing what רב הונא held. רב הונא would not sit on a bed with a ספר תורה on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רב הונא thought sitting on the same bed as a ספר תורה was not respectful to the ספר תורה, then laying a ספר תורה on the bier with his body would go against his view. That is why רב חסדא said not to do it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This story is a source for the הלכה that one may not sit on a bed or bench where a ספר תורה is lying.

phrases.english: As Rav Tachlifa said:
I saw Rav Huna
who wanted to sit on his bed,
and there was a Torah scroll lying on it,
and he turned a jug over on the ground
and placed the Torah scroll on it.
Evidently he holds:
it is forbidden to sit on top of a bed
on which a Torah scroll is lying.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב תַּחְלִיפָא: אֲנָא חֲזֵיתֵיהּ לְרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב חסדא's claim in step 15 about what רב הונא held.
steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא's claim that רב הונא did not hold of putting a ספר תורה on the same bed as a person.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב תחליפא's eyewitness story of רב הונא moving the ספר תורה onto a jug before sitting on his bed.

steps.title: The bier won't fit through the door, so they plan to lower it from the roof
steps.stepSummary: The bier was too big for the doorway, so the people planned to lower it down from the roof.
steps.simpleTranslation: The bier would not go out through the door, so they thought to lower it by way of the roof.
steps.whatsHappening: The story moves on to a new problem: the bier is stuck. The people suggest a second plan, which רב חסדא will answer next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This repeats the pattern of the story: a practical plan is suggested, and רב חסדא will correct it based on honoring a חכם.

keyTerms.meaning: To lower down (as with a rope)

phrases.english: The bier would not go out through the door,
so they thought to lower it by way of the roof.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the funeral story with a new problem.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because the bier did not fit the door, they planned to lower it from the roof.

steps.title: רב חסדא: a חכם must be taken out through the doorway
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rejects the roof plan, quoting what he learned from רב הונא: a חכם's honor is to go out through the doorway.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said to them: This I learned from him: a חכם, his honor is to go out through the doorway.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא stops the plan to lower the bier from the roof. He quotes רב הונא's own teaching that a חכם is carried out through the doorway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lowering a body from the roof looks undignified. Once again, רב חסדא uses רב הונא's own teaching to decide how to treat רב הונא.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said to them:
This I learned from him:
phrases.notes: 'Him' means רב הונא himself.

phrases.english: A Torah scholar, his honor is through the doorway.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב חִסְדָּא, הָא גְּמִירְנָא מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the plan from step 17.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The plan to lower the bier from the roof.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A חכם's honor requires being carried out through the doorway.

steps.title: They plan to move him onto a different bier
steps.stepSummary: Since he must go through the door, the people planned to move רב הונא onto a smaller bier that would fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: They thought to move him from one bier to another bier.
steps.whatsHappening: The people try a third plan: switching to a bier that fits through the door. רב חסדא will answer this in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This plan tries to respect the rule from step 18 (go through the doorway) by changing the bier instead. The next step shows this also goes against a חכם's honor.

phrases.english: They thought to move him from bier to bier.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new plan after the roof plan was rejected in step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: They planned to transfer רב הונא to a different bier.

steps.title: רב חסדא: a חכם stays on the first bier
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rejects switching biers, quoting רב הונא: a חכם's honor is to stay on the first bier.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said to them: This is what I learned from him: a חכם, his honor is on the first bier.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא stops the plan to switch biers. He quotes רב הונא's teaching that a חכם should stay on the bier he was first placed on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Moving the body from bier to bier is not respectful. This is the third time רב חסדא answers using what he learned from רב הונא. The next step gives the source for this rule.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said to them:
This is what I learned from him:
A Torah scholar, his honor is on the first bier.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב חִסְדָּא, הָכִי גְּמִירְנָא מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the plan from step 19.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The plan to move רב הונא to another bier.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A חכם's honor requires staying on the first bier.

steps.title: Source from a פסוק: the ארון on a new cart
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב brings a פסוק about carrying the ארון on a cart as the source that a חכם stays on the first bier.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב יהודה said in the name of רב: From where do we know that a חכם's honor is on the first bier? As it says: 'And they set the ארון of God upon a new cart.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a source from the תנ״ך for רב חסדא's rule in step 20. It learns how to carry a חכם from how the ארון was carried.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חכם, who holds Torah inside him, is treated like the ארון that held the לוחות. The way the ארון was carried on its cart teaches how a חכם should be carried on his bier.

phrases.english: As Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
From where do we know that a Torah scholar's honor is on the first bier?
As it says: 'And they set the Ark of God'
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 6:3

phrases.english: upon a new cart.'

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: מִנַּיִן לְחָכָם שֶׁכְּבוֹדוֹ בְּמִטָּה רִאשׁוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the rule in step 20.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a חכם's honor is to stay on the first bier.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק in שמואל ב about placing the ארון on a cart.

steps.title: They break open the doorway and carry him out
steps.stepSummary: With every other option ruled out, they broke open the doorway and carried רב הונא out on his first bier.
steps.simpleTranslation: They broke open the doorway and took him out.
steps.whatsHappening: This is how the funeral problem ends. They widened the doorway by breaking it, so רב הונא could go out through the door on his first bier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This solution keeps both rules: he leaves through the doorway (step 18), and he stays on the first bier (step 20). They chose to damage the house rather than lessen the honor of the חכם.
steps.whatToRemember: A חכם's honor at his funeral: no ספר תורה on the bier if he did not hold of it, he goes out through the doorway, and he stays on his first bier, even if the doorway must be broken.

phrases.english: They broke open the doorway and took him out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the story by carrying out both of רב חסדא's rules.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: They broke the doorway so רב הונא could leave through the door on his first bier, keeping his full honor.

steps.title: רבי אבא's הספד: רב הונא was worthy of the שכינה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא opened his הספד by saying רב הונא was worthy of having the שכינה rest on him, but living in בבל prevented it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא opened his הספד for him: Our רבי was worthy that the שכינה should rest on him, but בבל caused it not to.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now quotes the opening words of רבי אבא's הספד for רב הונא. He praises how great רב הונא was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבא says רב הונא was great enough for the שכינה to rest on him. The only thing stopping it was that he lived in בבל and not in ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba opened his eulogy for him:
phrases.notes: 'Opened' here means he began his הספד with these words.

phrases.english: Our Rabbi was worthy
that the Divine Presence should rest upon him,
except that Babylonia caused it for him.
phrases.notes: He means living in בבל is what kept the שכינה from resting on him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the funeral story, the גמרא moves to the הספד for רב הונא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב הונא was worthy of the שכינה, and only living in בבל prevented it.

steps.title: A נביא Who Prophesied in בבל
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר חסדא (or רב חנן בר חסדא) challenges רבי אבא from the פסוק showing that יחזקאל received prophecy in the land of the כשדים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר חסדא objected (some say it was רב חנן בר חסדא): The פסוק says, 'The word of ה׳ came to יחזקאל son of בוזי the כהן in the land of the Chaldeans!'
steps.whatsHappening: Someone attacks רבי אבא's opening line in the הספד. He uses a פסוק that seems to show prophecy can happen outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבא said living in בבל stopped the שכינה from resting on רב הונא. But יחזקאל was in בבל, and the word of ה׳ still came to him there. So it seems that being outside ארץ ישראל does not block prophecy.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection (a challenge from a source)
And some say (a second version of who said it)
The land of the Chaldeans, which is בבל

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Chisda raised an objection,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַב חָנָן בַּר חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: and some say it was Rav Chanan bar Chisda:
"The word of ה׳ came [hayo haya]
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 1:3. Notice that the word 'came' is written twice. The גמרא will use that soon.

phrases.english: to Yechezkel son of Buzi the Kohen
in the land of the Chaldeans!"
phrases.notes: The land of the Chaldeans is בבל, which is outside ארץ ישראל. That is the whole point of the question.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אבא's statement in step 23 that being in בבל prevented prophecy.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that living outside ארץ ישראל prevents the שכינה from resting on a person.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: יחזקאל received prophecy while in בבל, so living outside ארץ ישראל cannot block prophecy.

steps.title: His Father Quiets Him
steps.stepSummary: The father, רב חסדא, taps his son with his sandal and scolds him for disturbing everyone during the הספד.
steps.simpleTranslation: His father tapped him with his sandal and said to him: Didn't I tell you not to trouble everyone?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a short story moment. The father stops his son from pressing the question in the middle of the הספד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father does not say the question is wrong. He only says that this is not the time to bother people with it. The real answer comes in the next step.

phrases.english: His father tapped him with his sandal,
he said to him:
Didn't I tell you
not to trouble everyone?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A reaction to the questioner from step 24. It quiets him but does not yet answer him.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The question should not have been raised in the middle of a הספד.

steps.title: יחזקאל Had Already Prophesied
steps.stepSummary: The doubled word 'היה' teaches that יחזקאל had already begun prophesying in ארץ ישראל, so his prophecy in בבל continued something that started there.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does the extra word 'came' mean? That it had already come before.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 24. It reads the doubled word in the פסוק closely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra 'היה' shows that prophecy had already come to יחזקאל before he was in בבל. His prophecy started in ארץ ישראל and only continued in בבל. So the rule from רבי אבא still stands: prophecy does not begin outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.whatToRemember: The doubled 'הָיֹה הָיָה' means יחזקאל already had prophecy in ארץ ישראל, so his case does not disprove רבי אבא.

phrases.english: What is meant by the extra "came"?
That it had already come.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Close reading of a doubled word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: יחזקאל's first prophecy came to him in בבל.
steps.terutzMaskana: יחזקאל began prophesying in ארץ ישראל, and in בבל he only continued.

steps.title: 'רב הונא Is Coming!'
steps.stepSummary: When רב הונא was brought to ארץ ישראל, רבי אמי and רבי אסי were told 'רב הונא is coming.' They thought he was alive and worried that they would again be overshadowed by him.
steps.simpleTranslation: When they brought him up there, people said to רבי אמי and רבי אסי: רב הונא is coming. They said: When we were there, we could not lift our heads because of him. Now that we have come here, has he come after us?
steps.whatsHappening: The story moves to ארץ ישראל, where רב הונא was taken to be buried. רבי אמי and רבי אסי misunderstand the news.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In בבל, רב הונא's greatness was so far above theirs that they felt they could not 'lift their heads.' When they hear he is coming, they think he has followed them to ארץ ישראל. This shows how great they considered him.

keyTerms.meaning: They brought him up (to ארץ ישראל)

phrases.english: When they brought him up there,
phrases.notes: 'There' means ארץ ישראל, where they brought רב הונא for burial.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי אַמֵּי וּלְרַבִּי אַסִּי:
phrases.english: they said to Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi:
Rav Huna is coming.
They said: When we were there,

phrases.aramaic: לָא הֲוָה לַן לְדַלּוֹיֵי רֵישִׁין מִינֵּיהּ.
phrases.english: we could not lift our heads before him.
Now that we have come here,
has he come after us?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the הספד discussion and continues the story of רב הונא's burial in ארץ ישראל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים of ארץ ישראל saw רב הונא as far greater than themselves.

steps.title: Who Went Out to Meet the Coffin
steps.stepSummary: They learn it is only his coffin. רבי אמי and רבי אסי go out to meet it. There are two versions about רבי אילא and רבי חנינא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They told them: His coffin has come. רבי אמי and רבי אסי went out. רבי אילא and רבי חנינא did not go out. Some say: רבי אילא went out, and רבי חנינא did not go out.
steps.whatsHappening: The misunderstanding is cleared up: only רב הונא's coffin has arrived. The גמרא then tells us which חכמים went out to honor it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי and רבי אסי, who knew how great רב הונא was, went out to honor his coffin. The first version says רבי אילא and רבי חנינא both stayed home. A second version says that רבי אילא did go out and only רבי חנינא stayed.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't confuse the two versions. Both agree that רבי חנינא did not go out. They argue only about רבי אילא.

phrases.english: They said to them: His coffin has come.
Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi went out,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אִילָא וְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא לָא נְפוּק.
phrases.english: Rabbi Ila and Rabbi Chanina did not go out.
Some say:
Rabbi Ila went out,
Rabbi Chanina did not go out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clears up the misunderstanding from step 27 and tells how each חכם responded.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אמי and רבי אסי went out to honor רב הונא's coffin. There are two versions of whether רבי אילא went out, and in both versions רבי חנינא did not.

steps.title: Why some חכמים went out to meet the coffin
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why those who went out to meet רב הונא's coffin did so. It answers with a ברייתא that says people line up and say mourners' blessings for a coffin being moved from place to place.
steps.simpleTranslation: What was the reason of the one who went out? A ברייתא teaches that when a coffin passes from place to place, people stand in a line for it and say the mourners' blessing and words of comfort for mourners.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the חכמים who went out to meet רב הונא's coffin did so, and gives a ברייתא as their source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Going out to meet the coffin was not just a personal choice. A ברייתא says a coffin moved from one place to another gets the full honor of a funeral: a line of people, the mourners' blessing, and comfort for the mourners.

keyTerms.meaning: A line of people standing to honor the dead or comfort mourners
Words of comfort for the mourners

phrases.english: The one who went out, what is his reason?
phrases.notes: Whoever went out to meet the coffin in step 28, like רבי אמי and רבי אסי.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא:
A coffin passing from place to place —
they stand in a line for it
and they say over it the mourners' blessing
and the comforting of mourners.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the halachic basis for one side of the two versions mentioned in step 28.
steps.raayaObject: The behavior of the Sage who went out to meet רב הונא's coffin
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: a coffin moved from place to place receives a line and mourners' blessings

steps.title: Why the other Sage did not go out
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives the reason of the Sage who did not go out. Another ברייתא says that for a coffin moved from place to place, people do not line up or say mourners' blessings.
steps.simpleTranslation: What was the reason of the one who did not go out? A ברייתא teaches that when a coffin passes from place to place, people do not stand in a line for it and do not say the mourners' blessing or words of comfort.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא gives the source for the other side, the Sage who stayed home. It is a ברייתא that says the exact opposite of the first one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each Sage now has a ברייתא supporting him. The two ברייתות use the same opening words but reach opposite rulings, which sets up a contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who did not go out

phrases.english: The one who did not go out, what is the reason?
As it is taught in a ברייתא:
A coffin passing from place to place —
they do not stand in a line for it
and they do not say over it the mourners' blessing
or the comforting of mourners.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite source, for the other side of the two versions.
steps.raayaObject: The behavior of the Sage who did not go out
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: a coffin moved from place to place does not receive a line or mourners' blessings

steps.title: The two ברייתות contradict each other
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the two ברייתות contradict each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: These two ברייתות contradict each other!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the two sources it just quoted, because one says to line up and the other says not to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both ברייתות describe the same case, a coffin moved from place to place, yet give opposite rulings. Something must tell them apart.

phrases.english: They contradict each other!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the two sources quoted in steps 29 and 30.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two ברייתות about honoring a coffin moved from place to place
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same case gets opposite rulings, so the sources cannot both be right unless they speak about different cases.

steps.title: It depends on whether the skeleton is intact
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the first ברייתא speaks of a body whose skeleton is still whole, and the second speaks of one whose skeleton is no longer whole.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. Here it speaks of a case where the skeleton is still whole, and there it speaks of a case where the skeleton is no longer whole.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction by saying each ברייתא speaks of a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the skeleton is still whole, the body still gets the honor of a funeral, so people line up and say the blessings. If the skeleton has fallen apart, these honors are not needed.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no contradiction

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
Here — where his skeleton is intact,
there — where his skeleton is not intact.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 31.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each ברייתא speaks of a different situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות seemed to describe the exact same coffin
steps.terutzMaskana: Funeral honors depend on whether the skeleton is still whole

steps.title: רב הונא's skeleton was whole, but one Sage wasn't told
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא's skeleton was still whole, so he deserved the honors. The Sage who did not go out had not been told this.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב הונא's skeleton was still whole. The one who did not go out had not had this confirmed to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies the new rule to רב הונא and explains why one Sage still stayed home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the rule just given, רב הונא's coffin deserved full honor, so the Sage who went out was right. The one who stayed home did not disagree with the law. He simply did not know the skeleton was still whole.

keyTerms.meaning: They did not confirm it to him

phrases.english: And רב הונא's skeleton was intact.
The one who did not go out —
they did not confirm it to him.
phrases.notes: Nobody told him that the skeleton was still whole.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the distinction from step 32 to the story of רב הונא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the facts: the one who stayed home lacked information
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The Sage who stayed home might have held that רב הונא's coffin did not deserve honor
steps.terutzMaskana: Everyone agrees on the law. The Sage who stayed home had not been told the skeleton was whole.
steps.whatToRemember: A coffin moved from place to place gets a line and mourners' blessings only if the skeleton is still whole. רב הונא's was, and the Sage who stayed home had not been told.

steps.title: Where should רב הונא be buried?
steps.stepSummary: The Sages ask where to bury רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: Where shall we lay him to rest?
steps.whatsHappening: The story moves on. The Sages of ארץ ישראל ask where רב הונא should be buried.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a fresh question in the story. It sets up the decision that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: We will lay him to rest, bury him

phrases.english: They said: Where shall we lay him to rest?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the honor at the coffin's arrival to the question of burial.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The right burial place for רב הונא

steps.title: Bury him next to רבי חייא
steps.stepSummary: They decide to bury רב הונא next to רבי חייא, because both spread תורה among the Jewish people.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא spread תורה among the Jewish people, and רבי חייא spread תורה among the Jewish people.
steps.whatsHappening: The Sages answer their question by pointing out that רב הונא and רבי חייא shared the same great quality.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since both men spread תורה widely, it is fitting for them to rest side by side. The answer does not say 'next to רבי חייא' outright, but the comparison makes that clear.

keyTerms.meaning: Spread תורה widely, taught many people

phrases.english: רב הונא spread Torah in Israel,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי חִיָּיא רִיבֵּץ תּוֹרָה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל הֲוָה.
phrases.english: and רבי חייא spread Torah in Israel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the burial question of step 34.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Bury רב הונא next to רבי חייא, since both spread תורה

steps.title: Who will bring him into the cave?
steps.stepSummary: They ask who is fit to carry רב הונא into רבי חייא's burial cave.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who will bring him in?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the place is chosen, they ask who is worthy to carry רב הונא into רבי חייא's cave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumes that not just anyone may enter רבי חייא's burial place. This sets up רב חגא's answer.

phrases.english: Who will bring him in?
phrases.notes: He means into רבי חייא's burial cave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the decision to bury him with רבי חייא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who is fit to carry the coffin into רבי חייא's cave

steps.title: רב חגא volunteers and explains why he is fit
steps.stepSummary: רב חגא offers to carry רב הונא in. He says he had mastered his learning by eighteen and never had a seminal emission. He also served רב הונא and knew his deeds: once a תפילין strap flipped over, and רב הונא fasted forty fasts for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חגא said to them: I will bring him in. I had established my learning by the time I was eighteen and never had a seminal emission. I also served before him and knew his deeds. One day the strap of his תפילין turned over, and he sat forty fasts for it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חגא answers the question and explains both his own purity and how well he knew רב הונא's holiness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חגא gives two reasons. First, he himself is pure and learned enough to enter such a holy burial place. Second, as רב הונא's attendant he knew how holy רב הונא was. The proof is that רב הונא fasted forty times just because a תפילין strap turned the wrong way.

keyTerms.meaning: A seminal emission, which makes a person impure

phrases.english: רב חגא said to them:
I will bring him in,
for I established my learning

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֲוֵינָא בַּר תַּמְנֵי סְרֵי שְׁנִין
phrases.english: when I was eighteen years old
and I never had a seminal emission,
and I served before him,
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the letter in round brackets; either way it means 'I served him.'

phrases.english: and I know his deeds,
for one day there turned over for him
a strap of the תפילין
and he sat forty fasts over it.
phrases.notes: The black side faced the wrong way, and he fasted to make up for not being careful.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב חַגָּא: אֲנָא מְעַיֵּילְנָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 36.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב חגא will bring him in, because he is pure and learned and knew רב הונא's holiness firsthand

steps.title: רב חגא brings רב הונא into the cave and a pillar of fire rises
steps.stepSummary: רב חגא carries רב הונא into the cave. רבי חייא's son יהודה tells his brother חזקיה to stand up in honor of רב הונא. A pillar of fire rises, and רב חגא, frightened, stands the coffin up and leaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: He brought him in. יהודה was lying at his father's right and חזקיה at his left. יהודה said to חזקיה: Get up from your place, because it is not proper to lie here while רב הונא is standing. As he stood up, a pillar of fire rose with him. רב חגא saw it and was frightened. He stood up the coffin and went out.
steps.whatsHappening: The story from the last step continues: רב חגא carries רב הונא into רבי חייא's burial cave. Something miraculous happens inside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even in the grave, רבי חייא's sons show honor to רב הונא. One should not stay lying down while a great תלמיד חכם is standing. The pillar of fire shows how holy this place is, and it scares רב חגא.

phrases.english: He brought him in.
phrases.notes: רב חגא is the one bringing רב הונא's body into רבי חייא's cave.

phrases.english: Yehuda was lying at his father's right
and Chizkiya at his left.
Yehuda said to Chizkiya:
Get up from your place,

phrases.aramaic: דְּלָאו אוֹרַח אַרְעָא דְּקָאֵים רַב הוּנָא.
phrases.english: for it is not proper conduct, since Rav Huna is standing.
As he stood up,
a pillar of fire rose up with him.
Rav Chagga saw it and was frightened,
he stood up the coffin and went out.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַיְּילֵיהּ, הֲוָה גָּנֵי יְהוּדָה מִיַּמִּינֵיהּ דַּאֲבוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries out what רב חגא offered in step 37: he brings רב הונא into the cave.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Inside the cave, רבי חייא's sons honored רב הונא. A pillar of fire rose, and רב חגא stood the coffin up and left.

steps.title: Why Rav Chagga was not harmed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רב חגא was not punished by the fire because he stood רב הונא's coffin up as protection.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason he was not punished is that he stood up רב הונא's coffin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds its own comment to the story. It explains why רב חגא was safe even though he saw the pillar of fire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is an unspoken question: seeing such a holy sight could be dangerous, so why was רב חגא not hurt? The answer is that the merit of רב הונא, whose coffin he stood up, protected him.

phrases.english: And the reason that he was not punished
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets; either way it means 'punished.'

phrases.english: is because he stood up Rav Huna's coffin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the ending of the story in step 38.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Seeing the pillar of fire should have harmed רב חגא.
steps.terutzMaskana: Standing up רב הונא's coffin protected him.
steps.whatToRemember: The story of רב הונא's burial ends here. רב חגא was protected by רב הונא's merit.

steps.title: At רב חסדא's death, they plan to put a Torah scroll on his bier
steps.stepSummary: A new story begins. When רב חסדא died, people thought to place a ספר תורה on his bier.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב חסדא died, they thought to place a ספר תורה on his bier.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new story about רב חסדא's funeral. This line sets up a plan that will be challenged in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting a ספר תורה on the bier was meant as a special honor, showing that the dead man was full of תורה. The next step asks whether this fits רב חסדא.

keyTerms.meaning: His bier (the bed the body is carried on)

phrases.english: When Rav Chisda died,
they thought to place a Torah scroll on his bier.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story about a different Sage's funeral.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The plan was to honor רב חסדא with a ספר תורה on his bier.

steps.title: רבי יצחק rejects the ספר תורה plan
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק says no. רב חסדא himself did not approve of this practice in his lifetime, so they should not do it for him now.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said to them: Something this master did not agree with, should we get up and do it for him?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק pushes back on the plan from the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His argument is simple: honor a person the way he himself would want. Since רב חסדא did not hold of this practice, doing it at his funeral would go against his own view.

keyTerms.meaning: He did not hold of it, did not agree

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said to them:
A thing that this master did not agree with,
phrases.notes: 'This master' means רב חסדא himself.

phrases.english: shall we get up and do it for him?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַבִּי יִצְחָק: מִילְּתָא דִּלְרַבֵּיהּ לָא סְבִירָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the plan from step 40.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole plan to put a ספר תורה on רב חסדא's bier
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It goes against רב חסדא's own opinion from his lifetime.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches that we honor the dead the way they would have wanted, not just in the grandest way.

steps.title: They plan not to baste their torn garments
steps.stepSummary: The mourners thought they should not loosely sew up the tears they had made in their clothes.
steps.simpleTranslation: They thought not to baste their tears.
steps.whatsHappening: Still at רב חסדא's funeral, the people make a second plan. This line sets up רבי יצחק בר אמי's ruling in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Mourners tear their clothes for a death. The people thought that for such a great Sage they should leave the tears open and not even loosely stitch them.

keyTerms.meaning: To baste, to loosely stitch together

phrases.english: They thought not to baste their tears.
phrases.notes: Basting means rough, loose stitches that close the rip without fully repairing it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second plan at the same funeral.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The mourners planned to leave their tears unstitched.

steps.title: רבי יצחק בר אמי: for a חכם, one may baste once turning away from the bier
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק בר אמי rules that for a חכם, the mourners may baste their tears once they turn their faces away from behind the bier.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק בר אמי said to them: For a חכם, once they have turned their faces away from behind the bier, they may baste.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק בר אמי corrects the mourners. They may stitch their tears after a certain point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mourners thought the tears must stay open. He gives a clear time limit: for a חכם, basting is allowed once they turn away from the bier. So the plan from the last step is rejected.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר אַמֵּי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak bar Ami said to them:
For a Torah scholar,
once they have turned their faces away from behind the bier,
they may baste.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר אַמֵּי: חָכָם, כֵּיוָן שֶׁהֶחְזִירוּ פְּנֵיהֶם מֵאֲחוֹרֵי הַמִּטָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the plan from step 42 and gives the correct rule.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that the tears may not be basted at all
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The הלכה allows basting for a חכם once the mourners turn away from the bier.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical הלכה about when mourners for a תלמיד חכם may stitch their torn clothes.
steps.whatToRemember: For a חכם, mourners may loosely stitch their tears once they turn away from the bier.

steps.title: רבה בר הונא and רב המנונא are brought to ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: When רבה בר הונא and רב המנונא died, they were brought up to ארץ ישראל for burial.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבה בר הונא and רב המנונא died, they brought them up there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short new story: two more Sages were brought to ארץ ישראל to be buried.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like רב הונא earlier, these Sages were buried in ארץ ישראל. This line also opens the way for what the גמרא tells next about them.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי נָח נַפְשֵׁיהּ דְּרַבָּה בַּר הוּנָא וְרַב הַמְנוּנָא,
phrases.english: When Rabba bar Huna and Rav Hamnuna died,
they brought them up there.
phrases.notes: 'There' means ארץ ישראל.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי נָח נַפְשֵׁיהּ דְּרַבָּה בַּר הוּנָא וְרַב הַמְנוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story about the burial of two other Sages.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבה בר הונא and רב המנונא were brought to ארץ ישראל for burial.
